reason: The original baseline overlapped independently recorded virtual simulation and another Electron run. A prospectively fixed, single complete block controls that known difference without changing the registered relative budgets or retrospectively converting the previous failure into a pass.

A separate Electron observation ran 07:47:15.146Z through 07:47:27.166Z, overlapping baseline active.
Contemporaneous integration journal also records simulation, native/gallery and build activity during the original baseline period.
Original active RAM failure remains 292.546875 MiB versus 290.375 MiB; no retrospective pass is issued.

All 19 stable samples above 290.375 MiB occur between 5.09 and 7.09 minutes; none occur after 10 minutes. A 55.859 MiB reduction at 7.342 minutes spans the same five process IDs. These observations do not identify the cause.

limitations: This approves the prospective measurement method only. It does not approve performance or predict a passing result.
The new baseline may produce a different numerical MiB limit under the unchanged formula. Publish both the old and newly computed limits; do not describe the numerical limit as unchanged.
One sequential block with baseline observations first cannot eliminate time-order effects or uncontrolled user/system workloads. It is improved condition control, not a randomized causal attribution.
Working-set sums can count shared pages more than once and do not separate JavaScript retention, native/GPU allocation, garbage collection, compression or OS page reclamation.
Boundary-only process/compression/swap snapshots can reveal coarse condition differences but cannot reconstruct every transient event.
A structural observer error leaves the block incomplete. Preserve all partial evidence; it is not a performance pass or permission to select favorable profiles.
If the complete block fails, retain the failure. Repeating unchanged code until a passing observation is not approved.
